prompt: Problem 1 (Semi-supervised logistic regression). $(X_i, Y_i)$ i.i.d. with $Y \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\tfrac12)$; $X \mid Y=0 \sim N((-6,-6), \mathrm{diag}(5^2, 15^2))$ and $X \mid Y=1 \sim N((6,6), \mathrm{diag}(5^2, 10^2))$. Observe labeled $S_\ell = \{(X_i, Y_i)\}_{i\le n_1}$ and unlabeled $S_u = \{X_i\}_{i>n_1}$. Fit logistic model $P(Y=1\mid x) = \frac{e^{\beta_0 + \beta^T x}}{1 + e^{\beta_0+\beta^T x}}$; $(\hat\beta_0, \hat\beta)$ is the MLE on labeled data, and $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ solves $0 = \frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{i\le n_1} Y_i(1, X_i^T)^T - \frac1n\sum_{i\le n}\pi(X_i;\beta_0,\beta)(1, X_i^T)^T$ (using unlabeled data). Use the given R data-generation code (set.seed(1)).
parts: 1) Explain why the logistic model is misspecified in this setting.
2) Report $(\hat\beta_0, \hat\beta)$ on training data and the average test log-likelihood and classification accuracy.
3) Find a loss $L(\beta_0, \beta)$ such that $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ minimizes it.
4) Write an R function computing $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ via Newton-Raphson.
5) Report $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ and its average test log-likelihood and classification accuracy.
6) Plot the training data (labeled + unlabeled) with the three classification lines (from $\hat\beta$, $\tilde\beta$, and the MLE using all $xs, ys$).
notes: Prof. Zhiqiang Tan. Exam requires Problem 1 AND one of Problems 2-3. Self-contained simulation. Transcribed from extracted text.

prompt: Problem 2 (Fisher LDA vs PCA). $N$ observations from $K$ classes in $p$ dimensions; $x_i$ the $i$-th input row, $Y_i \in \{1,\dots,K\}$.
parts: (1) Show the total covariance decomposes as $(N-1)\Sigma_t = \sum_i (x_i - \hat\mu)(x_i-\hat\mu)^T = (N-K)\Sigma_w + (N-1)\Sigma_b$, with within-class $\Sigma_w$ and between-class $\Sigma_b$ as defined.
(2) Show Fisher's reduced-rank LDA, $\max_v \frac{v^T\Sigma_b v}{v^T\Sigma_w v}$, is equivalent to the eigenproblem $\Sigma_w^{-1}\Sigma_b v = \lambda v$.
(3) Generate 100 observations from each of three given Gaussian classes in $\mathbb{R}^{128}$ (means $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3$, common diagonal covariance).
(4) Write your own code for Fisher's reduced-rank LDA; visualize the data projected onto the first two directions, colored by class.
(5) Perform PCA; visualize the projection onto the first two principal directions, colored by class. Compare with (4) and explain the difference.
notes: Prof. Ying Hung. Self-contained simulation. Transcribed from extracted text.

prompt: Problem 3 (Engine block/head joint GP experiment). A 27-run experiment on eight factors $x_1, \dots, x_8$ (gasket thickness, contour zones, transition, bead profile, coining depth, deck flatness, load/deflection variation, head-bolt force variation), response gap lift $y$. (Do NOT use existing GP packages.)
parts: (1) For the GP model $Y(x) = \mu + Z(x)$ with correlation $\phi(h;\theta) = \exp(-\sum_{i=1}^8 \theta_i h_i^2)$, write the MLE expressions for $\mu, \theta, \sigma^2$ and report the estimates from the data.
(2) Write the BLUP and the (plug-in) predictive distribution.
(3) Report the leave-one-out cross-validation prediction error using the BLUP.
(4) Change to $Y(x) = \beta_0 + x_1\beta_1 + x_6\beta_2 + Z(x)$ and repeat (2)-(3).
(5) Suggest a final model comparing (1) and (4) via suitable performance measures.
(6) For the final model, plot the BLUP as a function of $x_1$ with 95% predictive bands.
(7) Find the optimal settings of the eight factors minimizing gap lift, explaining the algorithm.
notes: Prof. Ying Hung. Dataset not in repo. Transcribed from extracted text.
